en: The master of speech cried aloud,
And sent the battle toward the other side,
The red Kyrgyz, the great fighter,
They made ready at every drumbeat,
The war drum deafened the ears,
They had it beaten with a thunderous roar.
Ears deafened and heads grew numb,
It bound mind and senses,
Blood sprayed like sparks,
Across the broad battlefield,
At the place of destruction,
Ozu Khan rode out to single combat.
Like a black boar, like a fox,
The battle cry of Khan Joloy,
The champion stood apart from the others,
He mounted a horse and went against the foe,
Who had ever known such a challenge?
Do not ask what Ozu was like,
It was the day the warrior went forth,
What could a solitary lamb do?
It was a day fought for a half-share of blood,
A day when Jadigöy raised a flame,
In this faithless world.
The day the treasure was gathered and stored.
Do not ask about his bloody words,
Dark-fated was the thought I conceived,
The very heart of harsh misfortune,
Of the punishment that struck your soul,
He has a head as large as a cauldron,
He has a khan who sets things in order,
When he attacks, he makes all sway,
When he surrounds them, he gives no respite,
He takes away the approaching host,
A khan remained who knew no settled place,
The lineage of the wild one,
Living while souls fought beside him,
One who drank and was never sated with blood,
One who spared no life in battle,
Who crushed their steel warriors,
Who crushed even the unmatched wise men,
Raised in the desert breathing poison,
Raised on the crag spilling blood,
Riding abroad and cutting off heads,
Breaking the people like a stallion,
Destroying the nation and throwing it into turmoil,
Making the earth quake with blood,
He himself was a bloodthirsty tyrant.
The great Soz who entered the earth,
Soz Khan, elder among the Kalmyks,
That Soz Khan was among the wrestlers,
Many kaldays stood around him,
My khagan came from the raiders,
Breaking fortune through his courage,
Concerning the third world,
The valor of his wrestlers,
Became known here upon the earth,
One who especially spared no life.
Chyng Tengir, his chosen commander,
Had ordered him to go.
The poor, scant Kyrgyz people,
He thundered, bringing them torment,
Taking up a spear of black steel,
His fury would not cease,
You assemble it with your own hands,
What is this precise tongue of yours?
You tear away what you cannot take by right.
For the unruly son and young warrior,
O Kyrgyz people of the Kyrgyz,
Seeing you safe and alive,
Circling and seizing your land,
You will not act this way now,
Your irredeemable evil,
The appearance of the battlefield,
Let me drive you from the battle,
A steadfast one who will not leave when followed,
Let me strike and shatter him,
What is it that you desire?
Let me set the midst in order.
He prevailed and stood upon the battlefield,
With an exceptionally cutting tongue,
With teeth and tongue like a bear,
With a tongue of black and poisonous venom,
He began to humiliate the Kyrgyz.
You are a warrior who entered the field,
They cast aside the place of safety,
Calling them lesser men like fishermen,
Laying your wicked one in the grave,
Even the broad-hearted hero grew weary of you,
In your tale are herds that migrated,
One day you will see what your words bring,
There will be a struggle with the rebel.
Speaking thus, he thundered,
His formidable bearing surpassed all others,
As he stood enraged,
The people understood in their hearts,
He roared like gathering mist.
Your sign has become known,
Ozu Khan, who brought devastation,
You grew arrogant, Koñorchun,
Your insolent tongue took hold,
Draining the champions,
Knowing those who faced you,
I shall envelop you like a horse’s ear.
If you lash out, dusty calamity rises,
If you encounter the unyielding marksman,
People speak of what the nation knows,
Stirring from the black stone,
I, Khan Ozu, surged ahead,
When I stood before the Khagan,
I put on the iron helmet,
Facing men, I rolled up my sleeves,
I was a man of youth,
Ozu Khan mounted his horse,
And as khan ruled the people,
Towering as he mounted the horse,
Living his life as a man,
What manner of wrath you displayed,
The outer peoples would not accept you,
The tribal people of the Black Kyrgyz,
Calling your warriors ninety strong,
Finishing all who faced you,
Calling the numerous host ninety,
Saying the hero Kakharbay would triumph,
Saying I would continue the struggle,
From the idol that made him bow,
Your deeds will ride back upon you,
I shall go wrapped in resolve,
Accept what I desire,
May my joy brighten my face.
Its dense stitching stood out,
Thickly wrapped and firmly joined,
Covering the lofty warrior,
Wisdom came to my brave one,
Its patterned workmanship appeared,
The black Kyrgyz were an enemy people,
Who came to confront me head-on,
Burut, gather and let your thousands come,
You shall see how great your courage is,
Never sated in what he demanded,
He never ceased his grasping,
When two stood before him,
He broke and destroyed whoever encountered him,
Four stood exchanging insults,
Every sweep of it became a flame,
It was the time when the warrior was like an eagle,
Whoever went near would never return,
It was the time a brave hero defended the Kyrgyz,
Set upon grass, it sent fire racing,
His thrusting spear scattered embers,
It was a time when the Kyrgyz were left powerless,
It was the time the hulking Odu remained,
I shall spill the blood of an enemy,
I shall cast the boastful one into conflict,
O my Kyrgyz, my Burut people,
Let your courage descend upon the bloody field,
I have taken him as spoil,
Roaring in violent rage,
Thundered forth menacingly,
It was the moment to face Odu,
His true fury became apparent,
Despairing of his life, tiny as a fly,
That warrior Odukan’s,
At the place where he reeled away,
A man stood upon the black earth.
A storm raged at the mountain’s foot,
Leaving not a soul standing,
Against the venomous force of the multitude,
Against wrath massed like ice,
Known by the true crown,
Ebegey and Köböy, the two lions,
Now despairing of their lives,
No soul could withstand their might,
No one could equal their aspect,
Their true fury became clear,
Like Chyngyn, they despaired of life,
This Chinese Ozu Khan,
His might was a towering mountain,
He was master of the whole world.
It was an hour when the fighter’s soul burned,
His soul burned and caught fire,
When the black-headed one turned and spoke,
There was no calamity like this unto death,
It was a burning hour that came upon the Kyrgyz.
Death prevailed and bullets prevailed,
The extraordinary affliction was complete,
Ears heard it and eyes saw it,
There was no other champion like him.
Even Alymkan could not match him,
He was a youth beyond comprehension.
He created a great calamity,
She was a maiden written into fate,
He himself was true death,
He waited patiently and stood firm,
No life remained despite their pleas,
When his wrath struck,
None remained alive to be captured,
No room remained for those who marveled,
Among the brave, he was a hero,
Until the champion had seized them all.
Five thousand warriors prepared for single combat,
They darted like maidens from the cloth,
Those who met fought long,
All who encountered him,
Were dragged away as if by death.
Ebegey despaired of life,
And said this to hero Köböy,
When he could not recover his senses,
Hero Köböy offered wise counsel,
Whether called warrior or hero,
He had not burned our homes,
Both a champion and a hero,
In honor he was a lion,
He fought as long as his eyes could see,
A wise man among many warriors,
They truly rushed together in a roar,
Dear Köböy gave counsel,
He heartened the multitude of heroes,
His mind pondered for the khan,
A thousand days of calamity and torment,
Were built together with suffering,
Poured out in wrath,
Falsehood and futility,
The fighting champion observed it,
He swung himself against the sword,
His dear people cried out in grief,
Finding words of wisdom for the khan,
Finding sight in the black night,
They grappled more keenly than steel,
Sharpen your stirring tongue,
With wisdom and with the people,
He watched the enemy’s road,
The scouts’ brave flank was broken,
It was one wing of the brave men.
My heart lies over the earth like mist,
Ebegey and Köböy, the two heroes,
My plane trees thrust against the enemy.
Hero Kenen, the blue-maned one,
Glanced once upon this day,
Meeting one small as a louse,
Knowing the way, they acted as heroes,
Making your wish come true,
Making Ala-Too their land,
Unable to face the enemy,
They leveled him with the black earth,
Fortunate Seyrek awakened,
His true resolve would never turn back,
These two heroes among the Kyrgyz,
Ebegey and Köböy became heroes,
Hero Kenen, the blue-maned one,
He rushed like an albasty demon,
He swooped like a hunting bird.
From the beginning the mound was stirred,
They became friends for the hereafter,
Doing deeds beyond ordinary men,
Knowing the weightiest words,
He shattered what had been gathered,
